title: EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) Gap Assessment
framing: This is a gap assessment against the EU Cyber Resilience Act for a manufacturer of products with digital elements. It has three layers, each scored separately. The Annex I Part I product requirements are assessed for each product, and the Annex I Part II vulnerability handling requirements once for the organisation. The third layer covers conformity and obligations: the declaration, CE marking, conformity route and reporting. Each layer can be included or left out for an engagement.
sourceNote: The requirements are transcribed from Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act), OJ L, 20.11.2024. Layers P1 and P2 cover Annex I Part I points (2)(a) to (m) and Part II points (1) to (8), and each of those items carries the Official Journal wording next to the requirement as the assessor phrased it. The conformity layer draws on Articles 13, 14, 28, 29, 30 and 32 and Annexes II, V, VII and VIII. These items cite the relevant Article or Annex without quoting it, because each spans several provisions. The text is reproduced with attribution to the Official Journal of the European Union.
criticalCaveats: No harmonised standard has yet been cited in the Official Journal under the CRA, so presumption of conformity through a standard is not formally available. A 62443 certificate, or any other, does not amount to CRA conformity.
This assessment informs conformity but does not determine or certify it. The manufacturer, or a notified body where the product class requires one, remains responsible for the conformity decision.
Article 14 reporting under the CRA applies from 11 September 2026, and the full obligations apply from 11 December 2027. Readiness should be judged against the date that applies.
scoringNote: Each layer is scored on the conformance scale: In place, Partially in place, Not in place, Unknown or Not applicable.

setup.question: Which layers are in scope for this assessment?

options.label: Annex I Part I: product requirements (per product)
Annex I Part II: vulnerability handling (organisation)

setup.effect: Layers left out are not assessed, scored or reported.

setup.question: Classify the product against CRA Annex III / IV
setup.method: Pick the Annex III or IV category that matches the product to see the class it suggests. With no match, the product is Default.
setup.drives: The product class decides which conformity route the P3 layer expects: internal control or a notified-body route. The category match sets the class, so the consultant does not need to judge it in advance.
setup.flagMisclassification: A category matches although the class is set to Default. This changes the conformity route and is a common CRA error.

setup.question: Product under assessment (name / model)
setup.drives: Part I is assessed for each product, so record which product this covers.

layers.name: Annex I Part I: Product requirements
layers.summary: These are the essential cybersecurity properties the product itself must have.

layers.name: Annex I Part II: Vulnerability handling
layers.summary: The manufacturer's vulnerability handling processes apply across all its products.

layers.name: Conformity & obligations
layers.summary: This layer covers the formal conformity work: risk assessment, technical documentation, conformity route, declaration, CE marking and reporting readiness. The route depends on the product class.

layerInterlock: The declaration and CE marking rest on the technical and process requirements in P1 and P2. Assessed on its own, P3 checks the paperwork without showing that those requirements are met.

items.title: No known exploitable vulnerabilities
items.requirement: The product is placed on the market without known exploitable vulnerabilities.
items.rationale: A product placed on the market with known exploitable vulnerabilities puts every user at immediate risk, and this is the clearest failure the CRA targets. An OT device is rarely patched, so a shipped vulnerability can sit in a plant for years. Getting this right before market entry therefore matters more than in IT.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.
items.verbatimText: be made available on the market without known exploitable vulnerabilities;

items.title: Secure by default configuration
items.requirement: The product ships with a secure default configuration, with the ability to reset to original state (tailor-made products excepted by agreement).
items.rationale: Default configurations built for easy setup leave products exposed from the start, and OT devices are often deployed exactly as shipped. A secure default is often the only hardening a device receives.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.
items.verbatimText: be made available on the market with a secure by default configuration, unless otherwise agreed between manufacturer and business user in relation to a tailor-made product with digital elements, including the possibility to reset the product to its original state;

items.title: Security updates mechanism
items.requirement: Vulnerabilities can be addressed through security updates, including automatic updates by default where applicable, with user notification and an opt-out.
items.rationale: A product with no sound update mechanism cannot be fixed once a vulnerability emerges, and users are left with a device known to be vulnerable. In OT the mechanism must also let operators control the timing, since an unplanned update to a running process can do as much damage as the flaw.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.
items.verbatimText: ensure that vulnerabilities can be addressed through security updates, including, where applicable, through automatic security updates that are installed within an appropriate timeframe enabled as a default setting, with a clear and easy-to-use opt-out mechanism, through the notification of available updates to users, and the option to temporarily postpone them;

items.title: Protection from unauthorised access
items.requirement: The product protects against unauthorised access through appropriate control mechanisms (authentication, identity/access management) and reports possible unauthorised access.
items.rationale: Access control keeps unauthorised parties away from the product's functions. Shared or unauthenticated access is common in OT because it is convenient. Reporting attempted access also gives operators information they usually do not have.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.
items.verbatimText: ensure protection from unauthorised access by appropriate control mechanisms, including but not limited to authentication, identity or access management systems, and report on possible unauthorised access;

items.title: Confidentiality of data
items.requirement: The product protects the confidentiality of stored, transmitted or processed data, for example by state-of-the-art encryption at rest and in transit.
items.rationale: Confidentiality is a lower priority in OT than integrity and availability, but exposed credentials, keys and configuration still give an attacker the means to do harm. Protecting that data limits reconnaissance and reuse.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.
items.verbatimText: protect the confidentiality of stored, transmitted or otherwise processed data, personal or other, such as by encrypting relevant data at rest or in transit by state of the art mechanisms, and by using other technical means;

items.title: Integrity of data and configuration
items.requirement: The product protects the integrity of data, commands, programs and configuration against unauthorised manipulation, and reports corruptions.
items.rationale: In OT the integrity of commands, programs and configuration has the most direct effect on physical operation, since altered instructions move equipment. Detecting and reporting corruption stops a tampered device acting on false data.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.
items.verbatimText: protect the integrity of stored, transmitted or otherwise processed data, personal or other, commands, programs and configuration against any manipulation or modification not authorised by the user, and report on corruptions;

items.title: Data minimisation
items.requirement: The product processes only data adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary for its intended purpose.
items.rationale: Collecting only the data that is needed limits privacy exposure and makes the product less attractive as a target. A device that holds more data than its function needs carries more risk and more liability.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.
items.verbatimText: process only data, personal or other, that are adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary in relation to the intended purpose of the product with digital elements (data minimisation);

items.title: Availability and resilience
items.requirement: The product protects the availability of essential and basic functions, including resilience and mitigation against denial-of-service attacks.
items.rationale: Availability is the top OT priority because the product runs a physical process, and resilience to denial of service keeps it running under attack or load. If its functions fail under stress, the operator can lose control of the process as well as the service.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.
items.verbatimText: protect the availability of essential and basic functions, also after an incident, including through resilience and mitigation measures against denial-of-service attacks;

items.title: Minimise impact on other systems
items.requirement: The product minimises its own or connected devices' negative impact on the availability of services provided by other devices or networks.
items.rationale: A product that floods the network or misbehaves on it can degrade the services of other devices and networks. Limiting that impact stops one weak component affecting the systems around it.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.
items.verbatimText: minimise the negative impact by the products themselves or connected devices on the availability of services provided by other devices or networks;

items.title: Limited attack surface
items.requirement: The product is designed to limit attack surfaces, including external interfaces.
items.rationale: Every exposed interface and service is a possible way in, and OT devices often ship with far more enabled than a deployment needs. Limiting the attack surface is one of the few hardening measures that works even on constrained hardware.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.
items.verbatimText: be designed, developed and produced to limit attack surfaces, including external interfaces;

items.title: Incident impact mitigation
items.requirement: The product reduces the impact of an incident using appropriate exploitation mitigation mechanisms and techniques.
items.rationale: Exploitation mitigation techniques limit what an attacker gains even when a vulnerability is present, including flaws nobody has found yet. That is especially useful in OT products, which stay in service for many years.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.
items.verbatimText: be designed, developed and produced to reduce the impact of an incident using appropriate exploitation mitigation mechanisms and techniques;

items.title: Security logging and monitoring
items.requirement: The product records and monitors relevant internal activity (access to or modification of data, services or functions), with a user opt-out.
items.rationale: Security logging is the basis for detecting and investigating attacks on the product, and many OT devices log poorly or not at all. Activity the product does not record cannot be detected or proven later.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.
items.verbatimText: provide security related information by recording and monitoring relevant internal activity, including the access to or modification of data, services or functions, with an opt-out mechanism for the user;

items.title: Secure data removal
items.requirement: Users can securely and easily remove all data and settings on a permanent basis, and transfer them securely where supported.
items.rationale: Secure data removal stops a decommissioned or transferred product leaking configuration, credentials or network detail. OT equipment is often repurposed and resold over a long life, so this exposure is common and easily overlooked.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.
items.verbatimText: provide the possibility for users to securely and easily remove on a permanent basis all data and settings and, where such data can be transferred to other products or systems, ensure that this is done in a secure manner.

items.title: Vulnerability and component identification (SBOM)
items.requirement: The manufacturer identifies and documents vulnerabilities and components, including a software bill of materials covering at least top-level dependencies, in a machine-readable format.
items.rationale: A manufacturer cannot manage vulnerabilities or components it has not identified, and an SBOM shows what the product is made of. OT products are often built on layers of third-party and legacy code, and the SBOM can reveal exposure the manufacturer did not know it had.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.
items.verbatimText: identify and document vulnerabilities and components contained in products with digital elements, including by drawing up a software bill of materials in a commonly used and machine-readable format covering at the very least the top-level dependencies of the products;

items.title: Address vulnerabilities without delay
items.requirement: The manufacturer addresses and remediates vulnerabilities without delay, including via security updates, with security updates provided separately from functionality updates where technically feasible.
items.rationale: A vulnerability known but not remediated is a live risk in every deployed product. Addressing issues without delay, and separating security from functionality updates, lets operators take the fix without being forced to accept unrelated change to a running system.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.
items.verbatimText: in relation to the risks posed to products with digital elements, address and remediate vulnerabilities without delay, including by providing security updates; where technically feasible, new security updates shall be provided separately from functionality updates;

items.title: Regular security testing
items.requirement: The manufacturer applies effective and regular tests and reviews of the security of the product.
items.rationale: Vulnerabilities that the manufacturer's testing misses can be found by an attacker in the field. Regular security testing finds those weaknesses before the product is released.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.
items.verbatimText: apply effective and regular tests and reviews of the security of the product with digital elements;

items.title: Disclose fixed vulnerabilities
items.requirement: Once a security update is available, the manufacturer shares and publicly discloses information about fixed vulnerabilities (description, affected products, impact, severity, remediation), with justified-case delay permitted.
items.rationale: Disclosing fixed vulnerabilities lets users understand their exposure and apply remediation, and hiding them leaves operators unable to protect themselves. The justified-delay provision balances that against arming attackers before a patch can be applied.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.
items.verbatimText: once a security update has been made available, share and publicly disclose information about fixed vulnerabilities, including a description of the vulnerabilities, information allowing users to identify the product with digital elements affected, the impacts of the vulnerabilities, their severity and clear and accessible information helping users to remediate the vulnerabilities; in duly justified cases, where manufacturers consider the security risks of publication to outweigh the security benefits, they may delay making public information regarding a fixed vulnerability until after users have been given the possibility to apply the relevant patch;

items.title: Coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy
items.requirement: The manufacturer puts in place and enforces a policy on coordinated vulnerability disclosure.
items.rationale: A coordinated disclosure policy gives researchers and users a defined route to report issues, and gives the manufacturer a defined way to handle them. Without one, vulnerabilities are reported haphazardly or not at all.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.
items.verbatimText: put in place and enforce a policy on coordinated vulnerability disclosure;

items.title: Facilitate vulnerability reporting
items.requirement: The manufacturer takes measures to facilitate sharing of information about potential vulnerabilities, including a contact address for reporting, covering third-party components.
items.rationale: Making it easy to report vulnerabilities, including in third-party components, gives the manufacturer a fuller picture of its exposure. A missing or hidden reporting channel means issues go unreported until they are exploited.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.
items.verbatimText: take measures to facilitate the sharing of information about potential vulnerabilities in their product with digital elements as well as in third-party components contained in that product, including by providing a contact address for the reporting of the vulnerabilities discovered in the product with digital elements;

items.title: Secure update distribution
items.requirement: The manufacturer provides mechanisms to distribute updates securely, so that fixes and mitigations reach users promptly, automatically where applicable.
items.rationale: A fix that cannot be delivered securely and reliably protects nobody, and a compromised update channel is itself a supply-chain attack. Secure distribution gets the fix to the deployed product intact.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.
items.verbatimText: provide for mechanisms to securely distribute updates for products with digital elements to ensure that vulnerabilities are fixed or mitigated in a timely manner and, where applicable for security updates, in an automatic manner;

items.title: Timely, free security updates with advisories
items.requirement: Available security updates are disseminated without delay and, unless otherwise agreed for tailor-made products, free of charge, with advisory messages informing users of relevant action.
items.rationale: Timely, free security updates with clear advisories let operators apply a fix with confidence, and charging for security updates would leave some users unprotected. In OT, the advisory detail lets an operator schedule the update safely around the process.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.
items.verbatimText: ensure that, where security updates are available to address identified security issues, they are disseminated without delay and, unless otherwise agreed between a manufacturer and a business user in relation to a tailor-made product with digital elements, free of charge, accompanied by advisory messages providing users with the relevant information, including on potential action to be taken.

items.title: Cybersecurity risk assessment
items.requirement: A cybersecurity risk assessment for the product is carried out and documented, and drives which Annex I requirements apply (Art 13(2)).
items.rationale: The risk assessment decides which Annex I requirements apply to the product, so without it the manufacturer cannot know what it must meet. The rest of the conformity work builds on it.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.

items.title: Technical documentation (Annex VII)
items.requirement: The manufacturer draws up and maintains the technical documentation required by Annex VII, kept for 10 years or the support period.
items.rationale: Technical documentation is the evidence that the product meets the requirements, and authorities can demand it for ten years. A manufacturer that cannot produce it cannot demonstrate conformity, however secure the product is.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.

items.title: Correct conformity assessment route
items.requirement: The manufacturer applies the conformity assessment procedure appropriate to the product's class (internal control, EU-type examination, or full quality assurance) per Annex VIII.
items.rationale: The conformity route depends on the product's class. Applying the wrong route, for example self-assessing a product that needs a notified body, invalidates the conformity claim, so the correct route is a precondition for a valid declaration.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.

items.title: EU declaration of conformity
items.requirement: A written EU declaration of conformity is drawn up per product and kept available to authorities (Art 28).
items.rationale: The EU declaration of conformity is the manufacturer's formal legal claim that the product meets the CRA. Without it, the product cannot lawfully carry CE marking or be placed on the market.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.

items.title: CE marking
items.requirement: The CE marking is affixed to products satisfying the applicable requirements.
items.rationale: CE marking is the visible sign of conformity that allows the product to be sold on the EU market. Affixing it without the underlying conformity work is a false declaration, and a product without it cannot reach the market.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.

items.title: Support and update period
items.requirement: A support period is determined and communicated, during which vulnerabilities are handled, reflecting the expected product use.
items.rationale: The support period sets how long the manufacturer will handle vulnerabilities. OT products stay in service for decades, so this obligation is demanding. An unclear or short period leaves operators exposed once support ends.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.

items.title: Vulnerability reporting readiness (Art 14)
items.requirement: The manufacturer can report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents to the CSIRT/ENISA within the CRA's early-warning and notification timelines.
items.rationale: The CRA sets tight timelines for reporting actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents, and a manufacturer without a process cannot meet them. Manufacturers are often least prepared here, because it needs an operational process as well as product properties.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.

items.title: User information and instructions
items.requirement: The product is accompanied by the information and instructions to users required by Annex II (secure use, support period, reporting contact).
items.rationale: Users can only operate a product securely if they are told how, including its support period and reporting contact. Without that information, a secure product can still be deployed insecurely.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.
items.reference: Annex II (information and instructions to the user)

items.title: Due diligence on third-party components
items.requirement: The manufacturer exercises due diligence on integrated third-party components so they do not compromise the product (Art 13(5)).
items.rationale: A product depends on the security of the third-party and open-source components built into it, and the manufacturer has a duty to exercise due diligence over them. Weak components often undo a manufacturer's own good practice.
items.evidencePrompt: Record the evidence and the basis for the conformance state.

_relatedWork: The deep CRA assessment the supplier screener's regulatory section routes into. Part II overlaps 62443-4-1 (secure development / vulnerability handling) - candidate cross-references, sourced from both requirement texts.
_classificationNote: Product classification uses the verified Annex III/IV lookup (shared/cra-product-classification.json), not a free choice. The lookup derives class -> conformity route. Annex III/IV are classification inputs, not assessable items; only Annex I content is scored.
seriesContext: The Cyber Resilience Act is an EU Regulation, so unlike a standard it applies directly, and conformity is a legal obligation for products with digital elements placed on the EU market. It sets essential requirements for the product itself and for the manufacturer's vulnerability handling process, and it requires certain incidents to be reported. Harmonised standards that would give presumption of conformity are still being developed, so this assessment works from the Regulation's own requirements.
_contentNote: 13 + 8 + 9 items across three independently-scored layers. Coverage verified against Annex I: Part I has exactly 13 lettered requirements and Part II exactly 8 numbered ones. Selectable layers; product classification drives the conformity route.

docx.coverSubLine: EU Cyber Resilience Act: indicative gap assessment
docx.docDescription: EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) indicative gap assessment
docx.layersSentence: Three layers were assessed separately: the Annex I Part I product requirements, the Annex I Part II vulnerability handling requirements, and the conformity and obligations layer. They are reported side by side and are not combined into a single CRA score, because a product with strong security but unfinished conformity work is not ready for the market.
docx.keyDatesNote: The CRA's Article 14 reporting obligations apply from 11 September 2026 and the full obligations from 11 December 2027. Readiness should be judged against the date that applies to each finding.
docx.misclassFinding: The product may be misclassified. The matched Annex III/IV category indicates a higher class than the one set, which changes the required conformity route. A later section sets out the finding.
docx.howToRead: Each requirement is judged In place, Partially in place or Not in place. Unknown reduces coverage and confidence, and Not applicable requirements are excluded. The Annex I requirements are quoted in the Regulation's own words. The conformity obligations each span several Articles, so they are phrased by the assessor and cite the Article or Annex. The Recommendations section lists every open gap with its evidence, impact, recommended action and owner.
limitations: The consultant sets the conformance state of each requirement on the three-point scale (Not in place, Partially in place, In place), based on the evidence gathered. The conformance index for each layer is shown for context only. Unknown answers reduce coverage and confidence, and Not applicable requirements are excluded. A requirement that is Not in place is reported as a floor finding and is never averaged away.

This is an indicative gap assessment against the EU CRA. It is not a conformity assessment and does not certify the product. The Annex I essential requirements are reproduced from Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 as published in the Official Journal of the European Union, and the Regulation text governs. No harmonised standard has yet been cited in the Official Journal under the CRA, so presumption of conformity through a standard is not formally available. A 62443 certificate, or any other, does not amount to CRA conformity. The manufacturer, or a notified body where the product class requires one, remains responsible for the conformity decision.
docx.blockerTail: cannot be lawfully CE-marked or placed on the EU market until those obligations are met, however strong its technical security.

docx.multiOrgSentence: The organisation-wide obligations (the Annex I Part II vulnerability handling process, Article 14 reporting readiness and component due diligence) were assessed once for the manufacturer and apply to every product. The Annex I Part I product requirements and the remaining conformity obligations were assessed for each product. The layers are reported side by side and are not combined into a single CRA score.
